'''Alexander Chigogidze''' ({{lang-ka|ალექსანდრე ჩიგოგიძე}}; 1 January 1955 – 14 December 2014)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://csitoday.com/2014/12/dean-alex-chigogidze/ |title=Dean Alex Chigogidze |publisher=CSI Today |date= |accessdate=2015-07-09}}</ref> was a Georgian-born [[General topology|general topologist]]. Chigogidze is best known for his book ''Inverse Spectra'',<ref name="google1">{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uaIrAAAAYAAJ |title=Inverse Spectra - Alex Chigogidze |date=2008-08-25 |accessdate=2015-07-09|isbn=9780444822253 |last1=Chigogidze |first1=Alex |publisher=Elsevier Science }}</ref> in which he passed on to the next generation of topologists
the results of the Fedorchuk -Schepin Topology seminars held at the Moscow State University during the 1980s. The book also contains important contributions Chigogidze made in the area of General Topology and Geometric Topology (of Bing-Borsuk type). In the area of General Topology, Chigogidze developed  extension theory for noncompact nonmetrizable spaces. In the area of Geometric Topology, Chigogidze introduced  grading to shape theory by 
developing a theory n-Shape where n is an arbitrary integer. This was a major addendum to the existing n-Homotopy theory.

After graduating from [[Tbilisi State University]], he became a research associate at Moscow University, moved on to become an associate professor and full professor at the [[University of Saskatchewan]] (Canada), and at the [[University of North Carolina at Greensboro]] where he was the H.Barton Excellence Professor and served as Head of the Mathematics Department.<ref name="Libres.uncg.edu">{{cite web|url=http://libres.uncg.edu/ir/uncg/clist.aspx?id=65 |title=A. "Alex" Chigogidze, UNCG NC DOCKS (North Carolina Digital Online Collection of Knowledge and Scholarship) |publisher=Libres.uncg.edu |accessdate=2015-07-09 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150710084332/http://libres.uncg.edu/ir/uncg/clist.aspx?id=65 |archivedate=2015-07-10 }}</ref> 
He served as the Dean of Science & Technology at the City University of New York, [[College of Staten Island]].<ref name="CSI Today">{{cite web|url=http://csitoday.com/2015/05/memorial-service-for-alex-chigogidze/ |title=Memorial Service for Alex Chigogidze |publisher=CSI Today |date=2015-05-01 |accessdate=2015-07-09}}</ref>

Throughout his mathematical career, he published over 100 papers and two books.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://at.yorku.ca/i/a/a/l/90.htm | title=Alex Chigogidze (1955-2014) | publisher=Topology Atlas | accessdate=8 September 2016 | archive-date=4 March 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304044608/http://at.yorku.ca/i/a/a/l/90.htm | url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Life==
Alexander Chigogidze was born in [[Tbilisi, Georgia]] on January 1, 1955, to Tchola Chigogidze (a doctor) and Rusudan Chinchaladze (a music teacher).{{citation needed|date=September 2016}} He died on December 15, 2014.{{citation needed|date=September 2016}}

== Academic career==
Alex Chigogidze was a senior research associate at the Georgian Academy of Sciences and then an associate professor at Petrozavdsk State University, Russia. After graduating from [[Tbilisi State University]], he became a research associate at [[Moscow State University]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.csi.cuny.edu/administration/academicaffairs/pdf/message.pdf |title=Information Update |accessdate=June 25, 2015 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141113230044/http://www.csi.cuny.edu/administration/academicaffairs/pdf/message.pdf |archivedate=November 13, 2014 }}</ref> where he received the esteemed [[Doctor of Science]] degree. He moved on to become an Associate and Full professor at the [[University of Saskatchewan]] (Canada).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://issuu.com/college-of-staten-island/docs/eye_on_csi_spring_2015/12 |title=Eye on CSI - Spring 2015 issue by CUNY College of Staten Island |publisher=ISSUU |date= 7 May 2015|accessdate=2015-07-09}}</ref>

===Moving to the U.S.===
In 2003, Chigogidze was offered the opportunity to be head of the Mathematical Sciences Department at the [[University of North Carolina at Greensboro]] (UNCG). There he was named an H. Barton Excellence Professor.<ref>{{cite web |author= |url=http://m.news-record.com/teachers-staff/article_129dfc83-bbb5-57b9-b8d2-77f7b572164b.html?mode=jqm |title=TEACHERS / STAFF - Home - News-Record.com |publisher=M.news-record.com |date=2015-01-25 |accessdate=2015-07-09 }}{{Dead link|date=December 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref name="Libres.uncg.edu"/>  While at UNCG, Dr. Chigogidze completely redesigned the undergraduate and graduate programs. He single handedly advanced and implemented numerous courses, and acted not only as a professor and educator, but also as a top administrator of the Mathematics Department. These accomplishments garnered the attention the UNC Administration, and placed him as a prominent leader in [[mathematics education]]. The caliber of his achievements dramatically altered the potential and performance of the University of North Carolina's mathematical department and its research.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://csitoday.com/2011/04/new-dean-of-science-and-technology-dr-alex-chigogidze/#.VOkymSlH1GE |title=New Dean of Science and Technology – Dr. Alex Chigogidze |publisher=CSI Today |date= |accessdate=2015-07-09}}</ref>

He served as the Dean of Science & Technology at the City University of New York, [[College of Staten Island]].<ref name="CSI Today"/>

==Publications==
Chigogidze’s research interests were mainly related to [[topology]], [[functional analysis]], [[operator algebras]] and [[metric geometry]].<ref name="yorku1">{{cite web |url=http://at.yorku.ca/i/a/a/l/90.htm |title=Alex Chigogidze |publisher=At.yorku.ca |date=2014-12-15 |accessdate=2015-07-09 |archive-date=2016-03-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304044608/http://at.yorku.ca/i/a/a/l/90.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|volume=349 |issue=11 |pages=4537–4555 |doi=10.1090/S0002-9947-97-02059-X |year=1997 |last1=Chigogidze |first1=Alex |last2=Hofmann |first2=Karl H |last3=Martin |first3=John R |title=Compact groups and fixed point sets |journal=Transactions of the American Mathematical Society |doi-access=free }}</ref>

Throughout his mathematical career, he published over 100 papers, as well as being referenced in the ''Encyclopedia of General Topology'' By K.P. Hart, Jun-iti Nagata, J.E. Vaugha.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=JWyoCRkLFAkC&q=A.+chigogidze&pg=PA106 |title=Encyclopedia of General Topology - K.P. Hart, Jun-iti Nagata, J.E. Vaughan |date=2003-11-18 |accessdate=2015-07-09|isbn=9780080530864 |last1=Hart |first1=K.P |last2=Nagata |first2=Jun-iti |last3=Vaughan |first3=J.E |publisher=Elsevier }}</ref>

"On a Generalization of Perfectly Normal Spaces, ''[[Topology and its Applications]]'', 1982.<ref>{{cite journal|title=On a generalization of perfectly normal spaces  |doi=10.1016/0166-8641(82)90003-7 |volume=13 |journal=Topology and Its Applications |pages=15–20|year=1982 |last1=Chigogidze |first1=A |doi-access=free }}</ref>

==Author==
In 1996, his book "Inverse Spectra", was published. A powerful method used in many areas of topology, the notion of an inverse spectra was originally introduced by [[Lefschetz]].<ref name="google1"/>

Dr. Chigogidze was on the editorial board of the JP Journal of Geometry and Topology, and also on the Tbilisi Mathematical Journal. 

==Death==
Chigogidze died in New York City on 15 December 2014.<ref name="yorku1"/>
